summary: Ryoshun Okubo is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1973–1983). He served as Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism at Waseda University (~1998) and as director of Taimon Kenkyūkai (attested 2007).
Ryoso Matsushita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Daishun Ueyama. He held an appointment as a lecturer (講師) at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).

Ryota Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies (doctoral coursework) and served as a graduate student researcher (院生研究員) at Toyo University (attested 2015). He was also a researcher at the Shinran Buddhist Center (attested 2015).

Ryotai Hatai (1883–1974) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held a post at Kyoto University (1929–1943) and served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (~1953–1974), teaching Gadjin Nagao and Ryogon Fukuhara.

Ryudo Fujii specializes in Indology and philosophy, having studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. Fujii held posts with the JSPS (attested 2003), Kokushikan University (attested 2010), and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).

Ryugen Taga is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1953–1955). At Rissho University, he served as lecturer (attested 1961), associate professor (attested 1972), professor (~1974–2002), and president (~1992–1995).

Ryugen Tanemura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Nishogakusha University (attested 2013), the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014), and Taisho University as a specially appointed associate professor (attested 2014–2018).

Ryuichi Abe specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, having studied at Keio, SAIS, and Columbia. He served as professor at Columbia University (~1996–2005) before becoming Reischauer Institute Professor at Harvard University (~2005).

Ryuichi Kogachi is a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1989–1998). He held positions at Kyoto University as research assistant (~2000–2007) and associate professor (~2007–2021), and at its Research Centre for the Cultural Sciences (~2000).

Ryujo Yamada (1895–1979) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Tokyo Imperial University and under Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at Tohoku University (~1943–1979), Musashino University (~1958–1969), and Ryukoku University.
Ryuken Sato (1930–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar. In 2014, he was attested as professor emeritus at Taisho University and as an adviser at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Ryusei Keira is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Keira studied at the University of Lausanne under doctoral supervisor Tom J. F. Tillemans, completing a thesis by 2003.

Ryushin Uryuzu (1932–2015) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1951–1960). He held posts at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Center (attested 1962) and as professor at Kyoto Women's University (~1975–1998).
Ryusho Onami is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taishun Mibu. He served as a lecturer (講師) at Taisho University (attested 1985).

Ryuta Kikutani is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Kikutani held posts as a specialist researcher at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and at Kyoto University's Hakubi Center/Graduate School of Letters (attested 2020).

Ryutaro Tsuchida is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and completed doctoral studies at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (~1984–2012).
Ryuzan Nishimoto (1891–1974) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Chishu Kitagawa and Chijo Kitagawa in 1916.
Ryōkei Kaginushi (1926–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar and professor at Otani University (attested 1978 and 1987–1993), who taught Nobuyoshi Yamabe.

Ryūshō Hikata (1892–1991) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying under Junjirō Takakusu at the University of Tokyo (~1914–1917). He held a professorship at Kyushu University (~1928–1958) and a post at Fukuoka Women's University.
Ryūō Asahi (1856–1926) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Toji and Koyasan University.
